shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Currently I have 1 A, 1 C, 1 B - a perfectly even bundle. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A, 1 C, 2 B, which is less diverse and reduces utility since I'd have none of a good. I prefer to maintain variety, so this trade doesn't help me unless it improves balance.

Current inventory is balanced (1A,1C,1B). Trading away my only B for another A would make me 2A,1C,0B, which is less diverse and thus lower utility given my preference for variety. Rejecting to seek a more balanced trade.

This trade would leave me with 3 A, 1 C, 0 B — losing my only B entirely and creating a heavy imbalance, which hurts my variety-based utility more than gaining an extra A helps. I'd rather keep a balanced spread across all three goods.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, C, and B. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, creating an imbalance instead of variety. Since I value variety, this trade would decrease my utility.

I currently have equal amounts of A, C, and B (1 each). Trading away B for C would just shift the imbalance (2 C, 0 B) rather than improve variety, which goes against my preference for balanced holdings. I'd rather keep my even distribution or trade for something that increases variety, not decreases it.

Trading away my only B (giving me 0) to get a 3rd C creates a very unbalanced bundle (1 A, 3 C, 0 B). Variety preference means I lose value from having zero B while stacking up C. Better to seek a trade that keeps some balance, like trading A or C surplus for something I have less of.

Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of A, C, and B. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, creating imbalance and reducing variety, which lowers my utility given my preference for balanced holdings.
Current bundle is 1A/1C/1B, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for another A would make me 2A/1C/0B, which is less diverse and reduces utility since I'd have zero of a good.

Trading away my only B (going to 0) while gaining a third A creates a highly imbalanced bundle (3A, 1C, 0B), which is worse for variety-based utility than my current even spread. I'd rather keep some B and seek a trade that balances C instead.

Trading 1C for 1B would just swap which good I have 0 of (going from 1/1/1 to 1/0/2), not improving variety. I currently have equal amounts of all three goods, so this trade doesn't help me and would create an imbalance.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, C, and B. Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 0 B and 2 C, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety and equal distribution, this trade would not improve my bundle.

Currently I have 1 A, 1 C, 1 B - an even spread. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with 0 B and 3 C, creating a worse imbalance since I value variety. This decreases my utility rather than increasing it.

Currently I have 2 A, 1 C, 0 B - a very unbalanced bundle. Trading 1 A (which I have plenty of) for 1 B (which I have none of) moves me toward a more even distribution (1 A, 1 C, 1 B), increasing overall utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with 0A, 1C, 1B - trading away all of a good entirely is too extreme. A better trade would be 1A for 1B, preserving variety across all three goods while still gaining B.

Trading away my only C (which I have least of, tied with B at 0) for B would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, just swapping which good is scarce rather than improving variety. Since I value variety, I'd rather keep C and acquire B without giving up my only C, or negotiate a trade that doesn't zero out a good I have only one of.

Trading away my only A would leave me with 0 A and 1 B, just shifting the imbalance rather than improving variety. Current bundle (1A,2C,0B) would become (0A,2C,1B) - still uneven with a zero. I'd rather find a trade that gives me B without fully depleting A, or trade a C instead since I have more of those.
I currently have 0 B and 2 C, so trading a surplus C for a scarce B improves variety and balances my inventory to 1 A, 1 C, 1 B - increasing overall utility.
Giving up 2C for 1B would leave me with A:1, C:0, B:1 — losing all variety in C is too costly. A better trade would be 1C for 1B, keeping balance across all three goods.
Currently I have 2 A, 1 C, 0 B. Trading 1 A for 1 B gives me 1 A, 1 C, 1 B - a perfectly balanced bundle, which suits my variety preference much better than having 2 A and 0 B.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with 0A, 1C, 1B - trading a scarce good imbalance for another. Currently I have A:2, C:1, B:0, so B is my scarcest good and gaining 1 is valuable, but losing 2A entirely eliminates that good rather than balancing my variety. A better trade would be 1A for 1B to diversify without depleting A completely.

This trade would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, going from having 1 of my scarcest good to having 0 of another good, essentially just swapping which good is at zero. Since I value variety, I'd rather keep C (1) and gain B without giving up my only C, or find a trade that doesn't leave me at zero on any good. Current inventory has A:2, C:1, B:0 - trading away my only C to get my only B just shifts the imbalance rather than improving diversity."

Trading away my only A would leave me with 0 A and 2 C, reducing variety instead of improving it. I'd rather keep A and acquire B without giving up my sole unit of A, since that would create an imbalance (0 A, 2 C, 1 B) that's not better than my current diversified position. I'd prefer trades that don't zero out a good I only have one of.
I currently have 0 B and 2 C, so trading away 1 C for 1 B moves me toward a more balanced inventory (1 A, 1 C, 1 B), which increases utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up all my C (2) for just 1 B would leave me with A:1, C:0, B:1 - trading away my only diversified good for an equally scarce one at a bad ratio. Better to trade only 1 C for 1 B to balance my bundle while keeping some C.

Trading away my only A would leave me with 0 A and 1 B, 2 C - still uneven and I'd lose my sole unit of a good I have only one of, dropping variety further. Since I value variety, giving up my only A for B (going from 1-1-0 mix... actually A=1,C=2,B=0) would leave A=0,C=2,B=1, which is still unbalanced (two goods at extremes). Better to hold and negotiate for a trade that doesn't zero out A while still getting B, e.g. trading a C for B instead."

Current inventory is A:1, C:2, B:0, heavily skewed away from B. Trading a surplus C for a scarce B moves me toward a more balanced (1,1,1) bundle, which increases my utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up all 2 C for just 1 B would leave me with A:1, C:0, B:1 - trading a diverse holding for an even more skewed one. Better to give only 1 C for 1 B to balance my inventory (A:1, C:1, B:1), which maximizes variety value. This exact offer costs too much C.

I have only 1 C and 0 B. Trading away my only C for a B would just swap which good I have zero of, without improving variety - I'd go from (2,1,0) to (2,0,1), same imbalance. I'd rather keep C and acquire B without giving up my only C, or get B while keeping some C.

Giving up 2 A for 1 B would leave me with 0 A, 1 C, 1 B - trading away my most needed diversity good too heavily. A better trade would be 1 A for 1 B, keeping balance across all three goods.

Trading away my only C for B would leave me with 0 C, just swapping which good I'm short on. I'd rather keep C and acquire B without depleting C to zero, since variety matters and C is already scarce in my inventory.

Since I only have 1 A, giving it away drops me to zero in that good instead of improving variety. Better to seek a trade that gets me B without fully depleting A, or trade away a C instead.
